chunks: From him, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, concerning

A man who had intercourse with his wife in the month of Ramadan and could not find what he could give in charity to sixty poor persons—he said: He should give charity according to the amount he is able.

key_terms.أَهْلِهِ: his wife or family, here meaning his spouse
key_terms.سِتِّينَ مِسْكِينًا: sixty poor persons, the standard number in this expiation
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan, the time of obligatory sawm (fasting)
key_terms.مَا يُطِيقُ: what he is able to manage or afford

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he cannot afford the kaffarah for intercourse in Ramadan?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning one who had intercourse with his wife during the month of Ramadan and is unable to fulfill the full expiatory charity to sixty poor persons. The ruling states that he should give charity according to the extent of his ability, showing consideration of financial capacity in expiation.
